Question: The mean, median, unique mode, and range of a collection of eight integers are all equal to \(8.\) The largest integer that can be an element of this collection is
Solution:
Arrange the integers as \(x_1\le x_2\le\cdots\le x_8\), and let \(L=x_8\). The mean gives a total of \(8\cdot8=64\), while the range gives \(x_1=L-8\).

To bound \(L\), find how small the other entries could be. The first three entries are each at least \(L-8\). The median condition gives
\[
x_4+x_5=16.
\]
Since \(x_4\le x_5\), we have \(x_5\ge8\), so \(x_6\) and \(x_7\) are also at least \(8\). Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
64&\ge3(L-8)+16+8+8+L\\
&=4L+8.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(L\le14\).

The collection
\[
6,6,6,8,8,8,8,14
\]
has total \(64\), median \(8\), and range \(14-6=8\). Its unique mode is \(8\), which appears four times, more often than any other value. Hence the upper bound is attainable, and the largest possible integer is \(\boxed{14}\), choice D.
